teaser.text: Occidental Petroleum, or OXY, is chiefly an oil-and-gas producer. It earns additional income by moving, processing and marketing energy products, while building a newer business around carbon removal.

stock.title: OXY stock forecast
stock.meta_description: OXY's forecast weighs bear, base and bull cases against commodity prices, production, cash flow and debt.
stock.opening: OXY's probability-weighted price is $58.44 in October 2027, $59.99 in October 2028 and $62.57 in October 2029. OXY's outcome hinges on commodity prices, operating delivery and debt reduction.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains OXY's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The forecast sees limited weighted upside, with substantial downside if oil and gas weaken. The probability-weighted price is $58.44 in October 2027, $59.99 in October 2028 and $62.57 in October 2029, equivalent to total returns of negative 5%, negative 1% and positive 5% with dividends. By October 2029, the bear case reaches $28.78 while the bull case reaches $120.48, against today’s $62.38.
The bear case carries 30% probability. The base case carries 55%, and the bull case 15%. By October 2029, outcomes span $28.78 in the bear case to $120.48 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for OXY, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s $13.4 billion EBITDA in 2027 falls to $12.8 billion and $12.5 billion thereafter. The base case uses realized oil near $70, $67 and $66 per barrel, stable production near guidance and modest cost savings. Production rose from 1.223 million to 1.434 million BOE per day while costs fell from $10.48 to $8.94 per BOE. The bear case gives $8.8 billion, $8.1 billion and $8.2 billion as oil falls toward $55 and gas remains weak. The bull case gives $16.5 billion, $17.3 billion and $18.2 billion as oil stays near $80–$82, Midland productivity improves and savings persist. Each $1 WTI change affects pretax cash by about $240 million.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for OXY today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, divides the share price by earnings per share. A trailing P/E uses recent earnings; a forward P/E uses analysts’ expectations. The lower forward multiple means analysts expect earnings to improve. That is an assumption, not a promise: weaker oil prices or higher costs could leave the forecast denominator unmet.

dividend.title: OXY dividend: payout, cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: OXY's common dividend is $0.28 per share quarterly, or $1.12 annually; cash coverage depends on free cash flow, debt and commodity prices.
dividend.opening: OXY pays $0.28 per share each quarter, or $1.12 per share annually. Its cash coverage depends on whether cash from operations remains after capital spending and stock pay.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines OXY’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does OXY pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Berkshire’s preferred shares still sit ahead of common shareholders. Oxy paid a preferred-stock dividend in 2025, cannot voluntarily redeem those shares before August 2029, and faces redemption consequences if common payouts exceed specified limits. In August 2026, Oxy raised its quarterly common dividend to $0.28 per share, but management still ranked debt reduction ahead of continuous buybacks. The cash story therefore leads directly to CrownRock: growth returned before the balance sheet was fully repaired.

Dividends stay at $1.12 per share annually in the base case because the declared quarterly rate is $0.28 and no longer-term target exists. The bear case falls to $0.84, then $0.56, after a cut; the bull case rises to $1.20 and $1.28 as cash improves. The history of cuts after the 2020 collapse makes the downside possible.

blocks.heading: What is OXY’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Production rose while liquids realizations weakened, so higher output did not guarantee stronger economics. OXY’s real free cash flow per share, computed as cash from operations minus capital spending and stock pay, fell from 2023 through 2025 even as total production grew. Year-end 2025 net debt was $20,428 million. The dividend yield was 1.8%, while buyback yield was 0.0%.

Dividend yield shows what the regular payout amounts to at today’s price; it does not prove that the payout will survive a weaker oil cycle. Common shareholders also rank behind debt and Berkshire Hathaway’s preferred stock. Berkshire holds warrants for 83.9 million shares. Their $59.59 strike was below OXY’s October 18, 2026 share price, so exercise is economically attractive and could dilute each existing owner’s percentage.

earnings.title: OXY earnings: November 9, 2026
earnings.meta_description: OXY reports on November 9, 2026; the key test is Gulf production, sales volumes and any change to full-year guidance.
earnings.opening: OXY's next results are expected on November 9, 2026. Watch final production and Gulf sales volumes, including what was restored after the pipeline constraint.
earnings.closing: The full OXY memo answers what drives its business, how its rivals compare, who runs OXY, and what risks could shape its results.

paragraphs.text: Management’s 2026 promise is to keep production inside a tighter range while spending carefully and reducing costs. Its August outlook set the annual production and net capital-spending ranges shown below.

blocks.heading: How has OXY's revenue and profit changed over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Oxy’s earnings, revenue and diluted EPS rose sharply from March 2026. Management attributed the change primarily to higher realized crude prices, with higher liquids realizations and derivative gains helping, while lower domestic gas realizations partly offset them.

Cash from operations also improved while capital spending remained substantial. That is encouraging, but one quarter cannot establish a new earning rate. The specialist wants to see favorable prices persist, costs remain controlled and production hold up before treating the result as durable.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in OXY's November 9, 2026 results?

paragraphs.text: The November results will show whether the Gulf disruption was temporary or has changed OXY’s full-year delivery. Occidental scheduled its third-quarter results for November 9, 2026, followed by a conference call on November 10.

Investors should look for final production and Gulf sales volumes, the amount restored after the pipeline constraint, any change to full-year guidance, and any lasting effect on costs or cash flow. If onshore wells continue to offset offshore weakness, the annual target may survive. If they do not, the cause—pipeline access, maintenance, weather or field decline—will shape next year’s spending.
